lines: One man went 382 days without solid food.
Angus Barbieri did it under medical supervision.
His body burned stored fat for energy, day after day.
Doctors checked his blood and urine throughout.
Years later, he had kept a healthy weight of 89 kilograms.
So stored fat can fuel a body for a year, but only with doctors watching.

traceability.purpose: Hook: frame 0 shows the body itself and the claim's number (382 days) lands as a readout, so the scale of the question is visible before it is explained.

evidence.claim: Angus Barbieri was a Scottish man who fasted for 382 days, from 14 June 1965 to 30 June 1966.
Barbieri began his treatment in the hospital but for most of the 382 days lived at home, visiting the hospital for outpatient checkups, including blood and urine samples.
